title: Interpretable deep learning on liver cancer slides derives a prognostic tumour risk score
summary: A weakly supervised, interpretable deep learning framework on whole-slide images from 1125 hepatocellular carcinoma patients (Zhongshan) and 320 TCGA patients produced a tumour risk score that was an independent prognosticator in both cohorts. Risk activation mapping visualized prognostic phenotypes, and links with multi-omics, including FAT3 and RYR2 mutations, are associative. Retrospective analysis.
ai_technology: Weakly supervised interpretable deep learning on whole-slide images with a tumour risk score and risk activation mapping

evidence.tested: Independent TCGA cohort of 320 patients with survival analysis.
evidence.unknown: Causal meaning of the phenotypes and prospective utility are not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning derived a risk score and visualized prognostic pathological phenotypes.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
